statement: Two candles are lit at the same time. Candle P is $30$ centimeters tall and burns down $1.5$ centimeters per hour. Candle Q is $22$ centimeters tall and burns down $0.7$ centimeters per hour. After how many hours will the two candles be the same height?

choices.misconception: I added the burn rates, $1.5 + 0.7 = 2.2$, and divided the $8$-centimeter difference in height by $2.2$.
I divided the $8$-centimeter difference in height by Candle P's rate, $1.5$, instead of by the difference in rates, $0.8$.
I moved the $22$ to the other side without changing its sign, so I divided $30 + 22 = 52$ by $0.8$.

hints: Write each candle's height after $t$ hours as a linear function.

solutions.reliable: After $t$ hours, Candle P is $30 - 1.5t$ centimeters tall and Candle Q is $22 - 0.7t$ centimeters tall. Setting them equal: $30 - 1.5t = 22 - 0.7t$, so $8 = 0.8t$ and $t = 10$. Check: both candles are $15$ centimeters tall after $10$ hours.
solutions.elegant: Candle P starts $8$ centimeters taller but loses $0.8$ centimeter per hour more than Candle Q, so it closes the gap in $\frac{8}{0.8} = 10$ hours.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
